problem: Existing ObjectNav methods handle isolated single-goal navigation and lack a lifelong, structured memory usable for continual open-vocabulary goals. Open-vocabulary auto-labels are noisy and synonymous, and prior memory methods (GOAT) rely on predefined vocabularies.
motivation: Service robots (e.g. in hotels) must sequentially find many different objects in the same unseen environment, so scene information should be memorized and quickly queried. Raw open-vocabulary text labels are unreliable as memory keys, whereas visual and positional features can distinguish instances. Frontier selection should also use context and avoid revisiting areas.
key_idea: Store open-vocabulary detections in an explicit instance memory indexed by position, HSV scene and confidence descriptors with SuperGlue-based instance merging, and combine it with a distance, semantic and footprint probabilistic frontier scoring.
insight: The memory model is the core of lifelong performance: removing it drops HM3D lifelong SR from 68.1 to 56.1 and SPL from 33.8 to 26.0. LLM-based STOP verification mainly raises SR (61.3 without it vs 68.1). The probability-map exploration helps most in the first few goals, and its advantage shrinks as memory accumulates (66.8 vs 68.1 SR). In the single-goal ablation, removing the footprint term hurts most (SR 54.3 vs 58.2).
method: Frontier exploration: builds a 2D grid map from depth and pose, clusters frontiers with DBSCAN, and records tried frontiers to avoid oscillation.

Probabilistic frontier scoring: P(F) ∝ o_d + o_s + o_f, i.e. Gaussian distance term (thresholded), semantic room co-occurrence term from memory objects and predefined groups, and a negative footprint term for revisited areas.
Open-semantic preprocessing: Grounded-SAM2 autolabel (Florence-2 detailed caption), keyword filtering of noisy labels such as 'wall', and GPT-4o-mini synonym generation for the goal.
Memory descriptors: each entry stores label, image buffer, 3D position descriptor, HSV histogram scene descriptor and confidence C_i (based on center offset, depth and bbox area).

Instance matcher: computes S_m from HSV similarity and position distance; ambiguous scores trigger SuperGlue matching (threshold of 60 matched points); matched instances are merged, keeping the higher-confidence parameters.

Navigation and verification: KMP substring search over memory labels for the goal and its synonyms; greedy planner to the target position; 360° capture, GPT-4o probability fused with memory confidence (ω=0.5); failed candidates are removed from memory.

setting.backbone: Grounded-SAM2 (Florence-2-base) + GPT-4o (verification) + GPT-4o-mini (synonyms) + SuperGlue, all frozen
setting.action_space: low-level Stop/Move Forward/Turn Left/Turn Right/Look Up/Look Down, with a waypoint/frontier planner
setting.privileged: none (GPS/compass-style pose is given as input)

results: In lifelong ObjectNav OVAL reaches SR/SPL 68.1/33.8 on HM3D and 44.1/18.6 on MP3D, beating VLFM (53.7/30.6 and 35.1/16.7) and GOAT (59.2/31.2 on HM3D; N/A on MP3D). In standard ObjectNav it reaches 58.2 SR on HM3D and 41.1 on MP3D (best SR among the compared methods), but its SPL is below VLFM's (30.4 and 17.5).
limitations: Supports only ObjectNav and cannot handle multi-modal goal inputs.
Recognition degrades in dynamic, complex, fast-moving scenes.
Depends on GPT-4o calls and a large stack of models, giving about 1.14 FPS and low SPL in single-goal ObjectNav; the lifelong dataset is a simulated reordering of episodes with teleportation.
